claim: Scanning the full AAAI 2025 accepted-papers digest for code-generation/code-LLM/calibration/uncertainty keywords surfaces only two code-generation-adjacent entries — 'Calibrating Large Language Models with Sample Consistency' and 'AnalogCoder: Analog Circuit Design Via Training-Free Code Generation' — and no paper matching DPRC's specific niche of per-requirement/localized self-expressed confidence for code.
stance_target: novelty gap: DPRC's specific niche (per-requirement self-expressed code confidence) is not directly contested by any AAAI-2025 accepted paper found
scope_conditions: keyword search across full AAAI-2025 Paper Digest listing (hundreds of entries)
quoted_support: AnalogCoder: Analog Circuit Design Via Training-Free Code Generation ... we introduce AnalogCoder, the first training-free LLM agent for designing analog circuits through Python code generation.

claim: AAAI-2025-listed uncertainty/calibration papers found in the digest are overwhelmingly domain-specific to non-code areas (knowledge tracing, partial-label learning, multi-view clustering, trajectory prediction, motion capture, knowledge-graph reasoning), reinforcing that code-specific uncertainty/calibration is an under-served AAAI niche as of 2025.
stance_target: whitespace argument for DPRC: code-specific confidence calibration is not yet a crowded AAAI subarea
scope_conditions: AAAI 2025 accepted papers, keyword search on 'uncertainty'/'calibrat'/'confidence'
quoted_support: Uncertainty-Aware Knowledge Tracing model (UKT) which employs stochastic distribution embeddings to represent the uncertainty in student interactions

claim: 'Calibrating Large Language Models with Sample Consistency' is listed in the AAAI 2025 digest despite its own arXiv comment identifying it as AAAI 2024 — indicating secondary AAAI paper-year listings can be unreliable and should be cross-checked against primary arXiv/DOI metadata.
stance_target: reliability caveat for using secondary digest/blog sources to establish AAAI year-of-acceptance
scope_conditions: cross-referencing Paper Digest listing vs arXiv:2402.13904 metadata
quoted_support: Calibrating Large Language Models with Sample Consistency ... derive model confidence from the distribution of multiple randomly sampled generations, using three measures of consistency.
